chunks: Al-Husayn ibn 'Ubayd Allah informed me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya, from his father, from Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub, from Musa ibn 'Umar, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Maythami, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, from his grandfather, who said:

I asked Aba 'Abd Allah عليه السلام about a well into which a mouse or some other animal falls and dies, then dough is kneaded from its water: may that bread be eaten? He said: If the fire has touched it, then there is no problem in eating it.

key_terms.الدَّوَابِّ: animals or creeping creatures other than the mouse
key_terms.النَّارُ: the fire by which the bread is baked
key_terms.الْبِئْرِ: the well from which the water was taken
key_terms.الْخُبْزُ: the bread made from that dough
key_terms.الْفَأْرَةُ: a mouse, mentioned as an example of an animal falling into the well
key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm or objection; an expression of permissibility
key_terms.فَيُعْجَنُ: dough is kneaded using that water

ai.seo_question: Can bread made with water from a contaminated well be eaten after baking?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a jurisprudential ruling concerning water from a well into which a dead animal has fallen and which was then used in dough. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام states that if the bread made from that dough has been exposed to fire, there is no objection to eating it.
